s0_0.t: Hello, and welcome to Future Lab!

s0_1.t: This educational app has been made by Nuria Calvo, an English teacher at IES Goya, Zaragoza.

s0_2.t: In English, there isn't just one future. There are several, and each one tells us something different.

s0_3.t: Today you'll learn when to use will, be going to, the present tenses, the future continuous and the future perfect. Let's go!

s1_1.t: The form is easy: will, plus the infinitive without to. It's the same for every person. In the negative, we say won't.

s1_2.t: We use will for predictions and opinions, especially after I think, I'm sure, or probably. I think it will rain tomorrow.

s1_3.t: We also use it for decisions we make at the moment of speaking. The phone's ringing! Don't worry, I'll answer it.

s1_4.t: And for offers and promises. That bag looks heavy. I'll carry it for you. I promise I won't tell anyone.

s1_5.t: Careful! Never say: I will to go, or: she will goes. Just say: she will go.

s2_1.t: The form is: am, is or are, plus going to, plus the infinitive.

s2_2.t: We use it for plans and intentions: things we decided before speaking. I'm going to study medicine at university.

s2_3.t: We also use it for predictions based on evidence, something we can see right now. Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.

s2_4.t: In the negative: She isn't going to come. And in questions: Are you going to watch the match?

s3_0.t: Chapter three: will, or going to?

s3_1.t: Here's the key question: when did you decide?

s3_2.t: If you decide right now, use will. Oh no, there's no milk! I'll buy some.

s3_3.t: If you decided before, use going to. I'm going to buy some milk on my way home. I planned it this morning.

s3_4.t: And for predictions: an opinion takes will, but evidence you can see takes going to.

s3_5.t: I think Spain will win. But: look, they're three goals ahead! They're going to win!

s4_0.t: Chapter four: present tenses with a future meaning.

s4_1.t: We use the present continuous for fixed arrangements: plans with a time and a place, often with other people. I'm meeting Laura at six tomorrow.

s4_2.t: Imagine it's written in your diary. We're flying to London on Friday.

s4_3.t: We use the present simple for timetables and schedules. The train leaves at 8:15. The film starts at nine.

s4_4.t: So remember: arrangements, present continuous. Timetables, present simple.

s5_1.t: The form is: will be, plus a verb ending in -ing.

s5_2.t: We use it for an action that will be in progress at a specific moment in the future.

s5_3.t: This time tomorrow, I'll be lying on the beach. At nine o'clock tonight, we'll be having dinner.

s5_4.t: It's also a polite way to ask about someone's plans. Will you be using the car this evening?

s6_1.t: The form is: will have, plus the past participle.

s6_2.t: We use it for an action that will be finished before a certain moment in the future.

s6_3.t: It often goes with by: by Friday, by next year, by the time you arrive.

s6_4.t: By the end of June, I'll have finished all my exams. By 2050, scientists will have found a cure.

s6_5.t: And in the negative: Sorry, I won't have finished by then.

s7_0.t: Chapter seven: when, as soon as, until, and if.

s7_1.t: Here's a classic mistake. After when, as soon as, until, before, after and if, we use a present tense, not will, even when we're talking about the future.

s7_2.t: I'll call you when I arrive. Never: when I will arrive.

s7_3.t: As soon as she gets home, she'll text you.

s7_4.t: If it rains, we'll stay at home. And we'll wait here until the bus comes.

s8_0.t: Time for a challenge! Choose the right future for each sentence.

s9_1.t: Now you know all the futures: will, going to, the present tenses, the future continuous and the future perfect.

s9_2.t: This educational app was made by Nuria Calvo, an English teacher at IES Goya, Zaragoza. Now it's your turn: click the button and practise with the exercises. See you in the future!

q0.t: Question 1. Look at those black clouds! It, blank, rain.

q0_ok.t: Correct! We can see evidence right now, the black clouds, so we use going to.

q0_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: is going to. We can see evidence right now, the black clouds, so we use going to.

q1.t: Question 2. The phone's ringing. Don't worry, I, blank, it!

q1_ok.t: Correct! It's a decision made at the moment of speaking, so we use will.

q1_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: will answer. It's a decision made at the moment of speaking, so we use will.

q2.t: Question 3. Hurry up! The train, blank, at seven forty-five.

q2_ok.t: Correct! It's a timetable, so we use the present simple: the train leaves.

q2_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: leaves. It's a timetable, so we use the present simple: the train leaves.

q3.t: Question 4. This time next week, I, blank, on a beach in Greece.

q3_ok.t: Correct! It's an action in progress at a moment in the future: will be, plus -ing.

q3_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: will be lying. It's an action in progress at a moment in the future: will be, plus -ing.

q4_ok.t: Correct! It will be finished before a moment in the future, with by: will have, plus the past participle.

q4_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: will have finished. It will be finished before a moment in the future, with by: will have, plus the past participle.

q5.t: Question 6. I'll call you when I, blank, home.

q5_ok.t: Correct! After when, we use the present simple, not will: when I get home.

q5_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: get. After when, we use the present simple, not will: when I get home.
